channel.title: Frimley Fuel Allotments — Timeline of Events
channel.description: A fully sourced public records timeline tracking the proposed development of the Frimley Fuel Allotments woodland and Pine Ridge Golf Club for a new Frimley Park Hospital. Compiled from publicly available sources only.

item.title: 21 October 2026 — Pinkerton writes to McCarthy demanding hybrid planning application
item.description: Dr Al Pinkerton MP writes to FHFT Chief Executive Lance McCarthy urging the Trust to submit a hybrid planning application rather than a wholly outline one. Pinkerton argues that transport, access and highways are not secondary reserved matters — they go directly to whether Frimley Fuel Allotments is a viable location at all. A wholly outline application would allow the principle of development to be established while deferring the most consequential questions to later reserved matters applications. Pinkerton warns: "The planning process should be the point at which those questions are exposed to proper scrutiny — not a mechanism through which they are deferred." Source: Dr Al Pinkerton MP, letter to Lance McCarthy, 21 October 2026.

item.title: 17 October 2026 — Hogg newsletter admits access problems "undoubtedly real and present right now"
item.description: JHOSC Chair Cllr Trefor Hogg's ward newsletter confirms that the Transport and Access Study for the FFA site is only now "getting under way," with winter data still needed. He writes that access problems are "undoubtedly real and present right now" — directly contradicting his co-signed letter to NHS Frimley ICB of 4 July 2025, which asserted there would be "no negative impact on access." That letter was cited by the ICB when resolving not to undertake public consultation — a resolution the SCC Monitoring Officer has since confirmed was issued without authority and carried "no weight." The newsletter also confirms the scheme is moving from Strategic Outline Case to Outline Business Case stage, and that land purchases are expected before the Full Business Case is approved. Source: Trefor Hogg ward newsletter, 17 October 2026.

item.title: 14 October 2026 — SHBC Leader confirms monitoring officer ruled JHOSC letter had "no weight"
item.description: At Surrey Heath Borough Council's Full Council meeting, Council Leader Cllr Shaun Macdonald states that FHFT is "playing a little bit fast and loose with the facts" on school engagement. He then makes a statement of major legal significance: "The monitoring officer from Surrey County Council has confirmed that the chair and vice chair had no such authority to write on behalf of that body and therefore that letter had no weight in the decision-making process." The letter — co-signed by JHOSC Chair Cllr Trefor Hogg and Vice-Chair Cllr Carla Morson — was used by NHS Frimley ICB as the basis for its July 2025 resolution not to undertake public consultation. Macdonald also warns that if the proposal proceeds, "there will, on a mathematical and risk basis, there will be fatalities and serious injuries." Source: SHBC Full Council, 14 October 2026.

item.title: 13 October 2026 — ICO rules FHFT breached environmental information law on the day engagement closes
item.description: The Information Commissioner's Office issues Decision Notice IC-567662-H7C3 finding that Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust breached Regulation 5(2) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 by failing to respond within 20 working days to a request for all documentation, environmental reports, traffic and infrastructure reports, and risk maps relating to the site decision — submitted on 15 June 2026, the day before the preferred site was publicly announced. The ICO orders FHFT to provide a substantive response within 30 calendar days. Failure to comply may be treated as contempt of court. The notice is issued on the same day the 17-week public engagement closes — meaning residents completed their responses without access to documentation the Trust was legally required to disclose. Source: ICO Decision Notice IC-567662-H7C3, 13 October 2026.

item.title: 13 October 2026 — Pinkerton tells ITV of 50-acre sites "not even considered" — McCarthy confirms surveys still outstanding
item.description: ITV News broadcasts a report on the proposed new Frimley Park Hospital. CEO Lance McCarthy confirms traffic, transport and ecological surveys have not yet been completed. Dr Al Pinkerton MP tells ITV he is aware of "50 acre sites, which is what they claim they need, that haven't even been considered" — directly challenging the credibility of the 18-site selection process. When pressed whether the location is "still genuinely open to challenge," McCarthy answers: "Yes, absolutely." Source: ITV News, 13 October 2026.

item.title: 8 October 2026 — Windlesham Parish Council warns communities must not become "rat-runs" — criticises late engagement
item.description: Windlesham Parish Council submits a formal consultation response on behalf of the communities of Bagshot, Lightwater and Windlesham. Without opposing the principle of a new hospital, the Council raises significant concerns on transport and engagement. It demands traffic modelling covering the A322/M3 Junction 3 interchange, peak-period conditions, long-term demand, and displacement through all three villages, warning they "must not become rat-runs." It states that reduced car dependency must not substitute for proper road capacity assessment. On engagement: "That has not been our experience" — and: "Communication should not simply be about explaining decisions that have already been made." Source: Windlesham Parish Council, consultation response, 8 October 2026.

item.title: 12 October 2026 — 36 schools and 13,000 pupils: updated joint statement opposes FFA site on day engagement closes
item.description: On the day the public engagement exercise closes, school leaders from more than 36 schools covering 13,000+ pupils issue an updated joint statement opposing the FFA site. Their message: "We support the urgent delivery of a new Frimley Park Hospital. We do not support the Frimley Fuel Allotments site." The statement directly contradicts FHFT's public claim of close collaboration with schools: "public statements have suggested there has been close collaboration with school leaders when this has not reflected our experience." Dr Al Pinkerton MP says the case for the FFA site "has not been made." Sources: Local School Leaders joint statement; Al Pinkerton MP, Facebook, 12 October 2026.

item.title: 12 October 2026 — Public engagement closes — 10,000+ responses received, but traffic study has not yet started
item.description: The 17-week public engagement exercise closes. CEO Lance McCarthy tells BBC Radio Berkshire the programme received over 10,000 questionnaire responses. He confirms detailed traffic and transport analysis will not begin until November 2026 — after the engagement has closed — meaning residents raised transport concerns without access to any completed transport modelling for the site. HWRA members are quoted by BBC Surrey highlighting dangers to pedestrians and the community value of the woodland. Sources: BBC Radio Berkshire; BBC News, 12 October 2026.

item.title: 7 October 2026 — FHFT's final engagement email confirms ORS will "not make recommendations or decisions"
item.description: Four days before the engagement deadline, FHFT distributes an email confirming that Opinion Research Services (ORS) will prepare a report but will not make recommendations or decisions on the site. This directly contradicts FHFT's own FAQ, which states the site choice is "not final." The email also introduces the Green Book framework as reassurance — drawing attention to the fact that no business case has yet been approved. Source: FHFT email to members, 7 October 2026.

item.title: 29 September 2026 — CEO Facebook reel responds to "key issues raised" — five claims warrant scrutiny
item.description: CEO Lance McCarthy publishes a video responding to key issues raised about the proposed hospital. Analysis of the verbatim transcript identifies five claims that warrant scrutiny: a false dichotomy on the current site, unconfirmed funding presented as secured, an "independently assured" process with no assurance report published, a geographically misleading "closer to home" claim, and a framing that confirms the decision is treated as already made. Source: FHFT Facebook, 29 September 2026.

item.title: 26 September 2026 — JHOSC Chair's newsletter reports Annual Members' Meeting as promotional content — omits deprivation admission
item.description: JHOSC Chair Cllr Trefor Hogg's ward newsletter reports attending the Annual Members' Meeting but omits FHFT's own admission that a rival site scored better on deprivation. The newsletter also states the RAAC deadline as "by 2025" — a year that has passed and a date that appears in none of FHFT's official materials. Source: Trefor Hogg ward newsletter, 26 September 2026.

item.title: 22 September 2026 — At Annual Members' Meeting, FHFT concedes a better site for deprived communities existed — but was set aside
item.description: At FHFT's Annual Members' Meeting, a slide states: "One shortlisted site scored better on deprivation, but it could not be delivered because of size, aviation and ownership constraints." This is a formal, on-the-record concession that the Frimley Fuel Allotments is not the site best placed to serve communities with the highest health need. The evidence for setting aside the better-scoring site has not been published. Sources: FHFT Annual Members' Meeting, 22 September 2026.

item.title: 21 September 2026 — FHFT maildrop reaches local households — proposed site not mentioned
item.description: Frimley Health distributes an engagement postcard to households across its catchment area inviting residents to complete a questionnaire. The leaflet does not mention the Frimley Fuel Allotments, does not state that a preferred site has already been chosen, and does not mention woodland, green belt or the charity status of the land. Residents completing the exercise in good faith had no basis on which to assess the proposal's implications. Source: FHFT engagement postcard, received September 2026.

item.title: 18 September 2026 — CEO video rules out current site — contradicting FHFT's own record
item.description: CEO Lance McCarthy publishes a Facebook Reel stating the current site rebuild "wouldn't be complete by 2035" and that planning consent is "unlikely." Three things directly contradict this: (1) the government's independent assessment found FPH's RAAC planks serviceable to approximately 2040; (2) FHFT itself received planning approval for a four-storey building on the existing site in March 2023; (3) FHFT's own Site Selection Report shows FFA scored third out of four sites. Sources: Facebook Reel, Lance McCarthy, 18 September 2026; Mott MacDonald/DHSC, December 2025; SHBC planning records.

item.title: 12 September 2026 — Hundreds march in protest at FFA site choice
item.description: Hundreds of residents attend a peaceful protest walk organised by the Heatherside Ward Residents' Association (HWRA), gathering outside the existing Frimley Park Hospital. Dr Al Pinkerton MP attends. An HWRA spokesperson states: "The Trust's own experts ranked it third of four, and worst for the environment, yet it became the preferred choice." Sources: Surrey Live, 14 September 2026; Dr Al Pinkerton MP, Facebook, 14 September 2026.

item.title: 7 September 2026 — HWRA meets FHFT leadership — CEO apologises for engagement failures; CPO contradiction exposed
item.description: HWRA representatives meet CEO Lance McCarthy, SRO Caroline Hutton and Programme Director Alex White at Frimley Park Hospital. Key disclosures: McCarthy apologises more than once for not getting the engagement right. NHS England is confirmed to have reviewed and re-run the site selection process. FHFT acknowledges that compulsory purchase orders may be needed for transport — directly contradicting its stated rationale for selecting the site. FHFT confirms large areas of woodland would need to be removed. Source: HWRA Notes of meeting with FHFT, published 30 September 2026.

item.title: 6 September 2024 — Transport assessment completed and given to County Highways — junctions already at capacity
item.description: At the September 2024 JHOSC meeting, Interim Programme Director Cain Thomas discloses that a transport assessment has been completed and submitted to Surrey County Highways. The assessment finds that junctions near the preferred sites are "at capacity and requiring significant infrastructure upgrades." Thomas states the cost of road upgrades "would be part of the new funding envelope." The assessment has never been published. A request for its release has been submitted under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. Sources: JHOSC minutes, 6 September 2024; Surrey CC Highways (EIR request submitted).
